commands.name: standup
commands.description: Open a read-only status tab for every project with commits in the last N days (default 3)
commands.output: No git projects under /work have commits in the last 3 day(s).

tools.name: open_agent
tools.description: Opens a new terminal tab (or, if the user asks, a side-by-side pane) in `folder` and starts a Claude Code worker there whose first prompt is `brief`. The worker answers the user in that tab. Use it when the user asks for work or a status report about a specific folder. Write `brief` as a self-contained instruction: what the user wants, why, and what to report. Use read_only for status checks and reviews, resume to pick up the folder's last conversation, and worktree to run several workers on one repository without them touching each other's files. By default the worker ends its first reply with a one-line summary that list_workers shows here.

tools.name: list_workers
tools.description: Lists the workers spawn-pane opened: status (working, waiting for the user, needs the user, closed), age, tokens, estimated cost and each one-line summary. Use it when the user asks how their workers are doing or what they found.

tools.name: stop_worker
tools.description: Stops what a worker is doing, the way pressing Esc in its tab would: Claude ends its current turn (or declines the permission prompt it's waiting on) and the session stays open for the user. By name, id, or all busy workers. Use it for "stop X"; closing the tab is close_worker.

tools.name: answer_worker
tools.description: Answers what a worker is waiting on (list_workers shows it). For a permission prompt: approve presses Enter in its tab, choosing Yes; deny presses Esc. For a question it asked: reply types `text` into its tab and presses Enter ("continue", or the user's answer in their words). Use it when the user says to approve, deny, continue, or tell a worker something.

tools.name: close_worker
tools.description: Closes a worker tab spawn-pane opened, by its name (the folder name), its id, or all of them. Ends its Claude session.

tools.name: list_projects
tools.description: Lists the project folders in the user's workspace (absolute paths), most recently used first, with when each last had a Claude session and a git commit. Use it to match a name like "api" to its folder, and for requests like "the last five projects I worked on". Archives and backups are listed apart. Reads no file contents: anything about what's inside a project is a worker's job.

children: Ask the planner, e.g. "check the api project".

script: tool.call Bash rm -rf build && git push --force origin main
/standup → No git projects under /work have commits in the last 3 day(s).

notes: types ./types/index.d.ts declares on $: nothing (no EngineInterface member)
